resources.string: Save environment data to a file and restore it as a new environment
Create a new environment from a backup file
Backups may contain passwords, SSH keys, tokens and private files. Store them securely and import only backups you trust.
Includes the user home and its configuration files. Linux distributions and packages are excluded.
Includes distribution files, the package database, user home and configuration files.
Saves shell, startup command, environment variables and appearance settings for profiles linked to this environment.
The private working folder for this environment. Available when the folder exists.
A legacy working folder shared by several environments. Excluded by default.
Projects belonging to other environments may be included. Stop all environments that use this shared directory first.
Close sessions and processes writing environment files, and stop Userspace Linux before backup. Backup never terminates sessions or processes for you.
Use at least 8 characters. Passwords are never saved and cannot be recovered. Reenter after screen recreation.
Cannot retain access to this file. Choose another location using the Android document picker.
Copy of a legacy shared workspace
Creates new profile IDs and links them to the restored environment. Custom image icons use the default icon.
Imported shells and startup commands run when you later launch this environment.

Full integrity is checked during restore. Existing environments are never overwritten. Rootless data restores require a distribution installation afterwards. Imported shared workspaces become private copies.
Failed — check the cause and retry

Temporary files, download caches, running processes, sessions and scrollback are excluded. AVF disks, overwriting environments and automatic backups are not supported. Closing this screen keeps work running; cancellation requires an explicit action.
